newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency cool on Australia rice import hopes.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency cool on Australia rice import hopes.

text.p: Japan's Food Agency said on Wednesday that foreign rice imports this year would be based on domestic demand and local consumers' taste.
It said Australia, a major supplier of imported rice to Japan, should not raise its hopes too high of increasing its share of the Japanese market.

"Domestic rice demand and local consumers' taste will determine our import policy. We're not going to give special treatment to Australian rice," Yuki Takagi, director-general of the Food Agency, told Reuters in an interview.
"Australia should not be overly expectant," Takagi said.

On Tuesday, Australian Prime Minister John Howard said Japan's forthcoming import tender of 7,000 tonnes of rice on May 28 would give his country's rice growers a chance to expand their presence in the Japanese market.

The earlier-than-usual tender by Japan is good news for Australia, which being located in the southern hemisphere can export new season rice much earlier than other producers such as Thailand and the United States.
The Food Agency, Japan's sole importer of rice, wheat and barley, plans to carry out four import tenders under the simultaneous buy-and-sell (SBS) system this year.
During the current fiscal year, which started on April 1, Japan is obliged to import about 531,000 tonnes of rice under General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) deals concluded in 1993.
In the last fiscal year, Japan bought nearly 450,000 tonnes of foreign rice, of which 77,500 tonnes came from Australia.
Another agency official said local rice traders were complaining of the poor quality of Australian rice last year.

"Last year, the quality of Australian rice was damaged by colder-than-normal weather. If they (Australian growers) really want to boost market share here, they should improve quality first," the official said.
